rv.q: Despite the issues and people that Jack Was Kind calls to mind, Thorne and director Nicholas A. Cotz never quite get us to buy the story, either.
To get to those probing questions, though, you have to wade through the sometimes inarticulate, sometimes irrelevant ramblings of a character who, by her own admission, is less than camera ready.
As powerful as this battle may be, most of the conversation is emotionless.

cn.t: Tracy Thorne's 80-minute monologue about a wife's relationship with her husband draws mixed reviews. Critics praise the late-breaking reveal about the husband's true identity, but some find the one-person format lacks compelling drama.
